clue.text: Changed modus operandi and failed to protect single female

indicators.note: one word guarding another means it wraps around it, so the failure surrounds the next letters

parts.note: to fail, of a person or machine, can be to die
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: Someone altered their usual methods and so let down a woman living alone.
explanation.walkthrough: IF goes inside DIED after the first D, making DIFIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something altered or adjusted has been changed.

clue.text: One blowing their own trumpet?

parts.note: the idiom for a boaster is read literally: a player with a horn of their own

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a show-off is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player in a band literally plays an instrument they own.

clue.text: Doctor at home following adult's bleed

indicators.note: home comes after the adult, so it is written second

parts.note: A is the film-classification letter for adult
in means at home

explanation.surface: A GP visiting a grown-up at home lets blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drain a resource or to bleed it dry both mean to exhaust it.

clue.text: Delivery at no charge does often matter initially

parts.note: free means at no charge

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Whether delivery costs nothing often matters to online shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' looks like a parcel; here it means rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery from captivity is release, the liberty of being set loose.

clue.text: Flat race possibly unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished leaves the word without its end letter

parts.note: a race is an example of a sporting event

explanation.surface: A flat race may never be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat race' reads as horse racing; 'Flat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a level surface is smooth and flat.

clue.text: Punched, as criminal might be

definitions.meaning: struck with the hand, given a blow round the head
a criminal under arrest has handcuffs put on

explanation.surface: A crook gets hit, the way crooks sometimes do.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: struck with an open hand, and restrained in handcuffs by the police.

clue.text: A Parisian welcoming a fight in the dark

indicators.note: the French word lets the following letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: une is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman gets into a scrap at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts the article and the fight inside the French word for a.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being kept in the dark means being ignorant of something.

clue.text: Often got upset about king left behind

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the king's letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is often upset at being abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges OFTEN GOT, and 'about' puts that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind or abandoned has slipped from memory.

clue.text: Is husband following desperate character to get pastry?

indicators.note: the next pieces come after the comic character, so he goes first

parts.note: Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A husband trails a frantic figure in search of a bakery treat.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan, a famously hungry cowboy in the British comic The Dandy, gives DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet flaky pastry, often with fruit or custard.

clue.text: Government intended to dismiss a financial report?

parts.note: the state is the government of a country

indicators.note: dismissing a letter sends it out of the word it sat in

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: The authorities meant to brush aside an accounts document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss' removes the A from MEANT, leaving MENT. The question mark flags a definition by example: a bank sends one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bank or company issues a printed summary of accounts, a typical financial report.

clue.text: Very hot drink picked up — I cry out, almost

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word means reading it upwards, backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: almost cuts the last letter

parts.note: to call is to cry out

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a drink in sweltering heat and nearly shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns PORT into TROP; 'almost' cuts CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Equatorial climates are sweltering, so the word is used of extreme heat.

clue.text: In favour of wearing an item of protective clothing

indicators.note: the two letters of the article have the next word on them like clothes, so they go around it

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone backs putting on safety gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts the word for in favour of inside the article, as if the article wore it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a garment tied over the front to keep clothes clean while cooking.

clue.text: Approximately nothing for a country

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means approximately
nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Swapping roughly nothing for a whole nation sounds like a poor deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the large North American nation north of the United States.

clue.text: Teapots damaged with hole in — they could be chipped

indicators.note: the round letter is put in among the scrambled letters
damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, shaped like a ring, stands for a hole

explanation.surface: Broken teapots with holes in them might well be chipped china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges TEAPOTS, and an O goes in among those letters. 'Chipped' misleads towards crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: spuds are cut into chips, while chipped china is damaged.

clue.text: Horror film includes a good trap?

indicators.note: the film title holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: Carrie is a 1976 horror film from a Stephen King novel

explanation.surface: A scary film contains a decent snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' looks like a snare; a trap is also a light horse-drawn cart, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pony trap is a small two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Support PM at once with manic reforms

indicators.note: re-forms read as forms again, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A frenzied overhaul props up the prime minister straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges the letters of PM AT ONCE and MANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a piano or band backing a singer provides the support for the melody.

clue.text: Opinions stick

definitions.meaning: judgments or reviews of a work, as a critic offers
informal for harsh disapproval, as in taking stick

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: considered judgments of a work, and harsh fault-finding, informally called stick.

clue.text: Fast boats caught by ripples at sea

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Speedy craft get swept up by waves on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges RIPPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: fast sailing ships of the 19th century, like the Cutty Sark.

clue.text: Cross-country running finally leaving Nina tolerating exercising

indicators.note: exercising suggests moving about, so the letters are worked into a new order
the picked letter leaves the phrase it was in, so it is removed
finally points to the end letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Nina tolerates a run across fields as part of her exercise routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running finally' is G, which 'leaving' removes; 'exercising' rearranges the rest. 'Cross-country' looks like running, but means between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanning several nations, as a match between two national teams does.

clue.text: Pub in the right to get less stout

indicators.note: the pub is set inside the following letters

parts.note: taken as written
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Drinkers think a pub on the right will sell a weaker stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the dark beer; here it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means plump, so one less stout is slimmer.

clue.text: Picture that is about mother on alcohol

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes round the rest

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: in a down clue one word sitting on another is written above it

parts.note: ma is mother
gin is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: The scene of a mother on the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks mother above the drink in this down clue, and 'about' wraps the abbreviation for that is around both.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to picture something is to envisage it in the mind.

clue.text: Integrity from working within specific time

indicators.note: working sits inside the time word

parts.note: an hour is a specific time, as in the hour of reckoning
on means working

explanation.surface: Being upright comes from working within a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: moral uprightness or principle.

clue.text: First novel

definitions.meaning: earliest, the version from which copies were made
new and inventive, not seen before

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the earliest version, and fresh or inventive.

clue.text: Race to tee off before work

indicators.note: the irritation comes ahead of the work, so it goes first

parts.note: to tee someone off is to annoy them, to gall them
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A golfer hurries to drive off before getting down to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tee off' looks like golf; it is American slang for irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest pace, so to go at it is to race along.

clue.text: Holiday? Pack one's bags

definitions.meaning: time off work, as in annual or shore ...

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: authorised time off work, and to depart.

clue.text: Awful person staining cloth, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and written as another of the same sound

parts.note: a dyer colours fabric

explanation.surface: Someone who stains cloth sounds terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: Head working and working to take over Independent

indicators.note: the pair of words absorbs the next letter, holding it between them

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
on again means working

explanation.surface: A boss keeps working and working to absorb an independent rival.
explanation.walkthrough: I sits between the two ONs. 'Off one's onion' is British slang for mad, the bulb standing for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: the bulb vegetable is used for the human head, as in being off one's rocker.

clue.text: Get rid of characters in hotel — I'm in a temper

indicators.note: the letters sitting inside the phrase spell the word out

explanation.surface: An angry hotel guest wants someone thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The run runs from hotEL to TEmper.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to remove or eradicate something is to do away with it.

clue.text: Observe religious education with biblical book

parts.note: RE is the school subject religious education
Mark is the second Gospel of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A scripture lesson tells pupils to study one of the Gospels.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to observe can mean to comment, to say something in passing.

clue.text: Handlers of matches concerned with fire — see rioting after one's dropped

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: rioting is disorderly, so the letters are jumbled
dropped means let fall away, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: People fussing over a fire watch a riot after someone falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's dropped' takes I from FIRE SEE; 'rioting' rearranges what is left into FEREES. 'Matches' suggests things to strike, not games.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials who run football games control and oversee each fixture.
